content.title: Is Easter Monday 2026 a federal holiday in the US? What’s open and what’s closed after the holiday weekend
content.text: As the Easter holiday weekend comes to a close, many Americans are wondering what happens on Easter Monday (April 6, 2026), particularly whether banks, post offices, mail delivery, schools, and government services will operate as usual. Unlike some countries where Easter Monday is a formal public holiday, in the United States this day has a different status that affects operations nationwide.Is Easter Monday 2026 a federal holiday in the USEaster Monday is the day immediately following Easter Sunday, traditionally observed in many Christian communities around the world. Despite its significance in global Easter traditions, in the United States Easter Monday is not a federal holiday and is not included on the official list of federal holidays recognized by the federal government or the Federal Reserve.What this means in practice is that standard business and government operations usually continue on Easter Monday, unlike on holidays such as Christmas Day or Thanksgiving.Banks and financial services: Open or closed?Because Easter Monday is not federally observed, most banks and financial institutions will remain open for normal business hours on April 6. This includes deposit-taking, withdrawals, and in-branch customer services, though individual branches may have slightly varied schedules.Consumers who depend on in-person banking services or cash transactions should still verify hours directly with their local bank branch, as localized closures due to staffing or regional customary practices can occur even on non-holidays.Mail, shipping, and the US Postal ServiceBecause Easter Monday is not a recognized federal holiday, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) will operate normally on April 6, 2026. This means mail delivery services, package shipments, post office retail counters, and related services are expected to function as they typically would on a standard Monday.DMV and government officesState and local government services, such as Departments of Motor Vehicles (DMVs) and related agencies, typically remain open on Easter Monday. Because it is not a statutory holiday, most offices do not automatically close or adjust operations unless affected by unrelated regional closures or scheduled maintenance.This also applies to services like motor vehicle testing, licensing offices, and local administrative departments.Schools and local observancesPublic school calendars vary widely by district, and Easter Monday is not universally recognized as a school holiday. Some districts might remain open as part of regular spring schedules, while others could be on spring break or have planned closures depending on local educational calendars.Parents and students should check with their specific school district for precise schedules, as Easter week often overlaps with spring recess periods in many areas.Although not a federal holiday, Easter Monday features longstanding traditions in many US communities. One of the most recognized public events held on Easter Monday is the White House Easter Egg Roll, a historic annual celebration that draws families and visitors to the White House lawn for games and festivities, underscoring the cultural, if not official, prominence of the day.
